findings.problem: Line 6 drops the "like" from Jesus' comparison. The BSB says the one who hears and acts "is like a man building a house, who dug down deep and laid his foundation on the rock" (Luke 6:47-48). Line 6 says the one who hears and acts "builds on the rock, and when the torrent hits, that house doesn't shake." That turns the comparison into a plain statement about what the hearer does. It should keep the comparison, for example: that person is like a man who built his house on the rock.

Line 1 lists the poor, the hungry and the weeping (Luke 6:20-21) and the woes (Luke 6:24-26), then says "What you've got NOW isn't the whole story, because 'great is your reward in heaven' (Luke 6:23)." In the BSB, the reward in heaven in Luke 6:23 goes with those who are hated, excluded and insulted "because of the Son of Man" (Luke 6:22). That group isn't mentioned at all. The poor, hungry and weeping each get their own promise (the kingdom of God, being filled, laughing). Line 1 ties the 6:23 reward to groups the text doesn't tie it to.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open. Who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The Big Idea still leaves out the opening of the passage. In Luke 6:17-19 Jesus comes down to a level place, crowds come from Judea, Jerusalem, Tyre and Sidon to hear Him and be healed, and power comes from Him and heals them all. Line 1 starts with "here's the whole sermon in one box" and goes straight to Luke 6:20.
findings.question: In a Sermons passage, does "It covers the whole passage" mean the Big Idea must also mention the setting before the sermon starts (here the crowd and the healings in Luke 6:17-19), or is covering the sermon enough?
